title: Illustrative Nd/Dy deployment and supply-chain baseline

units.wind_intensity: kg of contained element per MW of new wind capacity
units.vehicle_intensity: kg of contained element per permanent-magnet passenger vehicle
units.material_flows: tonnes of contained Nd or Dy; never tonnes of finished magnets

production_share_proxies.scope: IEA stage shares have different denominators: magnet rare-earth mining, refining, and sintered magnet production. Applying the same shares to Nd and Dy capacity in a fixed basket is an explicit modeling assumption. These are not measured element-specific capacities or observed bilateral flows.

sources.citation: Cheng et al. (2025), Trade risks to energy security in net-zero emissions scenarios, Nature Climate Change; Supplementary Table 1.
sources.supports: Selected wind designs and passenger PM-car intensity ranges. The midpoint choice and this monthly disruption model are ours, not a full replication of the paper.

sources.citation: IEA (2026), Rare Earth Elements, Executive summary, 2024 production baseline.
sources.supports: China 60% mining, 91% refining, 94% sintered magnet production in 2024; separate stage denominators.

assumptions.deployment: 1 GW/year selected-design PM wind and 1 million PM passenger vehicles/year are a hypothetical constant portfolio, not a US or global forecast.
assumptions.network: Two capacity regions, China and Rest of world, with fungible global intermediate stocks. No asserted trade routes or supplier contracts.
assumptions.technology_mix: Fixed proportional Nd/Dy basket; no substitute motors or grades, no Pr/Tb, no explicit finished-magnet mass.
assumptions.operations: One-month stage lead times, 25% of a month of intermediate working stock, selected yields, 10% headroom, one month finished inventory; all uncalibrated assumptions.
assumptions.qualification: Additional non-shocked-region process capacity becomes usable after a six-month qualification/ramp lag; not an empirical qualification estimate.
assumptions.costs: 100 abstract units add 30%/25%/20% of baseline global output capacity in mining/refining/manufacturing, respectively, or two months finished stock. No real monetary cost-benefit conclusion is supported.
